answer: Persistent Work Ledger. Each identity accrues reputation only through logged task completions signed by counterparties; payouts unlock after a quartz delay period proportional to claimed capacity. Cloning yields fresh ledgers worth nothing, so an attacker must fund real work on every clone. Honest agents carry their history like a lantern through dark markets, while each clone costs full task-completion overhead before earning anything. New identities also need an ocean of verified counterparty signatures, making mass fabrication capital- and time-intensive.
